What if I told you that casinos are designed to make you lose track of time… and money?
Think about the last time you saw the inside of a casino.
Bright lights, flashing slot machines, music, and constant excitement.
But have you noticed something strange?
Many casinos have very few visible clocks.
And some gaming areas don't have windows.
Because the less attention you pay to time, the easier it can be to keep playing.
Instead of handing over cash every time you gamble, casinos often use chips or digital credits.
And spending a $100 chip can feel very different from handing someone a $100 bill.
Even though the value is exactly the same.
Casino games are designed with a mathematical advantage for the house.
Meaning that over time, the casino is expected to win.
So while you might walk in thinking you're just having fun…
The entire environment is designed to encourage you to keep playing.
You didn't know that about money.
